question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India deals with amendment in the Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 368**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part XX (Article 368)** of the** Indian Constitution **outlines the** constitutional amendment process.**
 
• This process protects the** Constitution of India's** sanctity and serves as a check on the arbitrary authority of the **Indian Parliament**.
 
• **Article 368** does not clearly forth the **legislative process** to be followed at various points of the change.
 
• **The Indian Constitution's Article 368 **deals directly with** constitutional amendments. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 365**

 
 
• ​According to **Article 365**, the **President** may declare that a situation has arisen in which the **State's government** cannot be carried out in accordance with the provisions of this **Constitution** if any State has failed to comply with or give effect to any directives provided in the exercise of the Union's executive power under any of the provisions of this **Constitution**.
 
 
 
• **Article 360**
 
 
• The **Indian Constitution's Part XVIII (Articles 352-360) **discusses the **Emergency Provisions. Article 360** specifically addresses the current financial crisis. The **Indian Constitution** contains three different categories of emergency provisions. The remaining two are:
 
 
• **National Emergency - Article 352**
 
• Emergency resulting from a breakdown of the state's constitutional machinery - **President's Rule - Article 356**
 
 
 
 
 
• **Article 355**
 
 
• "It shall be the duty of the Union to defend every State from external invasion and internal unrest and to ensure that the **government** of every State is carried on in conformity with the provisions of this **Constitution**," states **Article 355 of the Constitution.**
